pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING LISTENING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should we say the sounds in words, phrases, and sentences correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly
2. use words and phrases related to the theme in sentences correctly
3. listen for the main idea and specific details for effective communication
4. respond to information from an oral text

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension

Teach
• Focus skill: recognise sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː /, words, and phrases correctly.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we say the sounds in words, phrases, and sentences correctly?
2. How can we improve our pronunciation?
3. Why should we listen attentively?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
